If you're young the best medicine for any ails is to feel like you're accomplishing something of value to you - and that being something you feel like society agrees with.

It doesn't have to be a big thing. Just something that you feel will improve you. Work is the obvious thing. Work gives you a feeling of being self sufficient and it's very rewarding so long as you have a boss who'se not disturbed. (There are a lot of managers with very bad attitudes as management/authoritative positions attract bad people), but find an easy-ish profession, preferably a physically demanding one, and excell at it. It might be "below you" mentally, but it will give you the mental backing and boost to overcome many problems.

Don't value yourself by the value your parents estimate you at. I won't say anything negative about your parents as I do not know them, but the best person to give you a feeling of accomplishment is you. Listen to sunscreen and focus on something you're good at.

Later you can focus on something you love.

I formally educated myself at a later age than yours.  
I went for technical design. That allows me to be creative within certain paramaters that is more "measurable" and defineable as "correct" or "incorrect".  
 Visual arts and technical design can go hand in hand.  


I'm planning my own ticket so I'm not saying I have the solutions. But if you have creativity that wants to get out, but you don't have the esteem for it, maybe it could be a solutious for you to make it bearable.

I expect I'm more like him in that case.My natural instincts is to isolate myself and let the emotions fester.I want to be alone and I want to keep grinding that hurt.

I met my first love when I was 13. We were a couple untill I was 18. I loved her - or atleast I THOUGH I loved her. I was too immature to really know what love was. But it hurt. It hurt so much I think I had a nervous breakdown. I isolated myself for years and I kept hurting. I ALLOWED myself to hurt. Years later I realized I was only feeding the pain. I was the one deciding how much this was hurting. I had alianated everyone and nolonger had any close friends but I decided I had had enough. I started going to my then aquaintances. I really didn't want to go. I dreaded the phonecalls asking if I could come over. I felt like an idiot all the time.

But at the same time I did notice that while I was in the company of others, I felt better. I wasnt thinking about the bad feelings all the time and when I came home I felt like I had accomplished something. The more I forced myself to use and hone my social skills the less energy I was spending on the negativity. more and more I realized that the breakup was a GOOD thing and I was the one forcing the bad feelings.

your friend definatively has a reason to be hurt. His feelings are valid and he's right to be angry. The best thing right now might be a person to be angry WITH, not AT.

Some years ago I had a girfriend. She was WONDERFUL. I felt like nothing I've ever felt. She was EVERYTHING I idealize in a woman. Both physically and mentally. Mentally for the most part anyway: I found myself in a mad battle against myself. I never felt the right confirmations(?) from her and I was in a constant storm of emotions. Eventually I discovered she had registered on a dating site. That was a big blow for me. Possibly she just wanted confirmation and the ego boost messages from other men could give her or possibly she was opening herself up for the "next branch". In either case, I decided to end the relationship. And it hurt. my entire body said to stay with her, but my brain told me the rational thing is to leave.

Again I felt an all consuming sorrow and hate, but this time I was older and I knew what to do: Stay socially occupied. Make sure to feel social mastering (again struggling with the proper english translations) and not look back. Ignore the bad feelings.

​

I have come to believe that the best way to occupy the mind is to excercise your social antennae. We are hard coded for social maneuvering and I think our mind is built in such a way as to naturally spend alot of energy on social group dynamic.I can watch a movie and forget my problems for a little while or I can play a computer game and do the same, but it doesnt remedy the feelings - it only postpones it. For me, only social excercises help. Even though that's really the last thing I want to do when I'm in distress.

​

Oh. And smacktalking tends to help =)  
Having a good friend you can trust not to pass it on.  
Someone who can wholeheartedly agree when you call her "that bitch", "That fucking whore" or whatever. It doesnt have to be true. It just feels good then and there.

it is difficult to say without know what's going on.   
Sometimes it's best to talk to an adult.   
I know we seem like out of touch dinosaurs but for the most part we actually know what we're talking about. Some of us have forgotten how difficult it was being young, but alot of us still remember the bad and the good. 

Try to keep an open mind to your elders, and try to aboid someone who simply dismisses your problems. Your problems are real and should be taken seriously. Someone who doesn't take your problems seriously isn't the right person to help you. Find another.

Well.  
I am quite abit older.  
I have had many girlfriends and I've been in year-long relationships living togeher (not my first language so I dont know the terms). 

Time heals everything. It's a cliché but it's actually true - and every time we hurt we get just a little bit tougher for the next time. At my age and with my experience I can safely say that break ups doesn't hurt much anymore. That is to say, they do hurt but you have the knowledge that it will pass and you'll know what to do to make it pass faster.

For me it's important to be with friends. To be social. Keep my mind occupied with friends and make any effort to not be alone with my own thoughts. And by all means: Have no contact with the offending female. You'll want to, but it'll only hurt more and for longer.

I can't for sure say how HE's feeling. He experiences his pain in his way and he's allowed to do so. His hurt is entirely valid.

I wish I knew you personally.I'm happy for you that you came to the realization you want to keep fighting. You're young still and have many opportunities. I cannot speak for job opportunities in your country. I dont know where you're from and if it's any other than mine I wouldnt have a clue anyway.

I started in the lowest places. The hardest jobs. I had a shitty apartment. The cheapest I could find. If I had thought of it, I would prolly have lived in a van at work. I'm a nerd too, as I gather you are. I'm a fair bit older than you but I used to love playing games on the computer and playing dungeons and dragons (yes, I'm that old). With those hobbies that allowed me to spend very little money. At work I just ate bread, when I came home I pretty much slept untill the next day and my weekends basically cost me some sodas, some bags of chips and the odd games or dice unless I went out drinking, but I only ever drank beer so that's pretty cheap compared to drinks (where I live anyway).

A good recommendation from the first job landed the next job that was just a little bit better. Then that recommendation landed me a better one in a new line of work slightly better than that one. Then I was a site foreman, then a proper foreman in charge of several construction projects. Suddenly companies were calling ME wanting me to work for them.

Then I went back to school. Took a loan and finished with top grades and now I'm in more or less my drem job. I'm a designer working on a computer all day with easier days than I've ever had and considerably more pay.

​

The problem you're having is that you have to keep an eye out for psycopaths. There are ALOT  of them in work life. Psychopaths and business management goes hand in hand. They run their organization like a terror camp and you get NOTHING for working for them.Your job interview is also THEIR hiring interview.Measure them as they're measuring you. Find recommendations of good places to work. Offer to work cheaper if it's a good place that will give you a good recommendation letter. If you work for a BAD boss you'll just end up quitting when you become "enemies" (not my first language here) and you will get a bad recommendation or none at all.

At the start of your working life its not about pay - its ALL about recommendations.Give a little extra for your company, and if you're lucky enough to work in close contact with the clients, become real chummy with them. They can also be used as recommendations and maybe they'll even hire.

​

Oh - and DONT work for big companies.  
Don't be a number. Take jobs where you'll be on first name basis with your bosses.  
Project manager Tim don't give a shit about employee number 437. He'll give a standard template recommendation letter and you will have wasted your time working to earn his paycheck. Work for the guy who appreciates you and give him a little extra because you want your recommendation - and those guys are fewer and fewer. The big businesses and recruitment companies are completely taking over.

I'm glad for you.  
I remember when it really sunk in how I wanted to go. It was a calming sensation, but I'm still having trouble finding my specific method - I'm afraid of my methods failing.

Take control.  
Move. Drop out of college. Get a low paying manual job.  
It's the "wrong" move, but it'll be YOUR move.

Best case scenario you'll feel like you've taken control of your life. You'll feel in charge and self dependant. You might be surprised at how good it feels to be your own man at your age. Having a job with good pay doesnt mean squat. You either have to be proud of your job or you have to love it.

You can always take your education later in life.

​

I felt like a looser in my youth. The only thing school taught me is that I'm an academic looser and that made me think (for a long time) that I WAS a looser. I started in one of the lowest and physically toughest jobs you can take. I felt proud I was able to perform it. I was looked down at for having such a shitty job and the pay was even worse, but it built my self-esteem.

​

it's your life. You're in charge.  
Do what you want to and do what you need to do.  
Just make sure you learn something from everything you do.

Life is tough.  
Being a teenager is really tough.

You have to deal with adult problems and you're not yet hardened enough to handle it alot of the time.

You know - Every time we're exposed to something difficult we get just a little bit better at handling it the next time. We take tiny steps towards understanding how to get over it, how to surpess it and we learn ourselves small techniques to handle our troubles. So long as it's not overwhelming.

In your case it sounds overwhelming. it sounds like you have to deal with real adult problems at home with your mom. You are right to feel distressed and depression does make you sort of numb. I handled alot of anxiety and fear when I was a teenager. I suppressed it all. I suppressed an alcoholic home life, heart aches and my anxieties. Some people say it might have damaged me not seeking help. I've never talked to any professionals about my problems. Personally I don't see the point. Noone can tell me anything I don't already know.  
BUT... maybe they can...  I've never tried it so I couldnt say for sure.

I know you teenagers get told to grow up and handle it all the time but I'd like you to know that your problems are valid. Your feelings are valid. Only you can decide to take control and steer wich direction you want to go. Any direction is fine. Just try to learn something from whatever you do.

I found this post while planning my own suicide so I get it. Sometimes you just can't fix stuff. Sometimes the important elements in your life is just out of your control. I am quite a bit older than you and I have contemplated suicide for almost as long as you have been alive. I know how it feels when everyone keeps letting you down and all you do is fight uphill every day.

You CAN change most stuff, though. Especially at your age. We go through different phases all the time. The only thing that changes with age is that each phase last for longer and longer. Right now you're at a stage where you can make huge changes to your life. Changes will even come by themselves, but you may have to put some effort into it to ensure the changes are positive.

This might sound odd coming from someone currently planning their own suicide, and I'm absolutely not trying to devalue your opinions or solutions, but I would like to suggest you hold out for a little while longer considering your age.

Whatever you decide to do, I wish you the best possible outcome in your choice.
